description: Mouse movement is lost on frames shorter than 1 ms. CL_GetMouseMovement reads and clears the accumulated counts, then CL_MouseMove returns early when frame_msec is 0, so that frame's movement is dropped. At high frame rates (sub-millisecond frames) part of every flick disappears.
evidence: disassembly: the frame_msec test at 00553FBC follows the CL_GetMouseMovement call; reproduced by the reconstruction (tests/differential/test_client_mouse.py, frame_msec = 0 inputs: counts cleared, angles unchanged); the call is unconditional in the original

description: Mouse input is cursor based, not raw: the movement is the cursor's position change (GetCursorPos) and the cursor is put back in the window centre every frame (SetCursorPos). Windows pointer speed and "Enhance pointer precision" acceleration therefore apply to aiming, movement is in whole screen pixels, and a frame's movement is limited by the distance to the screen edge and, in fullscreen, by the window rectangle (IN_ClampMouseMove), so fast flicks are cut off.
evidence: reconstruction of IN_MouseMove, IN_ClampMouseMove, IN_RecenterMouse (tests/differential/test_win_input.py); the retail exe (t5mp) uses the same scheme (matched IN_MouseMove at 008BAE50)

description: Mouse acceleration measures speed per whole millisecond of frame time (counts / frame_msec, an integer), and the per-frame view speed caps (cgameMaxYawSpeed, cgameMaxPitchSpeed) use the same integer milliseconds. At high frame rates the rounding of frame_msec makes acceleration noisy and the caps uneven from frame to frame.
evidence: reconstruction (rate and cap computed from frame_msec); frame_msec is an unsigned int global

description: When aim assist is not initialized, AimAssist_UpdateMouseInput leaves AimOutput.meleeChargeYaw and meleeChargeDist unwritten, and CL_MouseMove copies those uninitialized stack values into the usercmd sent to the server. In normal play aim assist is initialized before the first usercmd, so no current caller is known to trigger it.
evidence: reconstruction of AimAssist_UpdateMouseInput (returns before AimAssist_ApplyAutoMelee, which is what writes the fields) and CL_MouseMove (copies them unconditionally)

description: WinVars_t has two layouts in the build: 32 bytes without lowLevelKeyboardHook (PDB type 0x8322) and 36 bytes with it (0xF689). Translation units were compiled against different versions of the header, so code built with the short layout reads sysMsgTime from offset 0x1C, where the full layout keeps lowLevelKeyboardHook. win_input.cpp uses the 36-byte layout.
evidence: PDB types 0x8322 and 0xF689; IN_MouseEvent reads sysMsgTime at g_wv+0x20 (007D8985); next global marker_win_wndproc at g_wv+0x24

description: Every mouse event outside menus calls CL_ShowSystemCursor(0), which reaches IN_ShowSystemCursor and calls ShowCursor at least once, a system call per mouse event per frame to hide a cursor that is already hidden.
m_filter smooths by averaging this frame's and the previous frame's movement, so the amount of smoothing (and the half-frame of added latency) depends on the frame rate rather than on time.
The AimInput built for mouse aim assist always says localClientNum = 0 instead of the client the command is for. Harmless with one local client (PC multiplayer); wrong for any other local client.
evidence: disassembly: MOV dword ptr [EBP-0x34],0 at 005545DF; reproduced by the reconstruction

description: Setting a bool, int or float dvar stores uninitialized stack into its value: the DvarValue built for the new value has only one member set (`enabled`, `integer` or `value`), and the whole 16-byte union is copied into current and latched, so 15 (bool) or 12 (int, float) bytes are garbage. Code that reads such a dvar through another member (a bool read as integer, a float read as a vector) gets garbage. Same in Dvar_SetIntFromSource (007C1E20) and Dvar_SetFloatFromSource (007C20A0).
evidence: differential harness: after IN_GamepadsMove changes gpad_present, bytes 1-15 of current and latched hold return addresses and a stack pointer, different in every build; after CG_SetThirdPerson (Dvar_SetInt on cg_thirdPerson, Dvar_SetFloat on cg_fov) bytes 4-15 do (tests/differential/harness.py dvar_undefined_bytes)

description: Only three aspect ratios exist: 4:3, 16:10 and 16:9. On auto, round(16 * height / width) picks one (10: 16:10, below 10: 16:9, above: 4:3), so 21:9 and 32:9 screens get 16:9 (the 16:9 view extents are drawn across the full width, stretched horizontally, and the Hor+ FOV stops at 16:9) and 5:4 and 3:2 screens get 4:3 (squashed). r_aspectRatio offers only the same three.
evidence: reconstruction of R_StoreWindowSettings (tests/differential/test_fov.py, modes up to 5120x1440); the retail exe (t5mp) does the same (matched R_StoreWindowSettings at 006D8240); CG_CalcFov takes cgs->viewAspect from vidConfig.aspectRatioWindow (CL_GetScreenDimensions)

description: The player's FOV setting (cg_fov_default) is limited to 65..80, as a 4:3 horizontal FOV: at most 96 degrees horizontal at 16:9 (80.7 at the default 65).
evidence: registration: _Dvar_RegisterFloat("cg_fov_default", 65, 65, 80, ...); CG_GetDefaultFovForView/CG_UpdateFov copy it into cg_fov; FOV mapping in docs/fov.md

description: The fixed FOVs ignore the player's FOV: deploying a weapon blends toward 55 and a turret forces 55, so with cg_fov at 80 the view narrows sharply on every deploy and turret. The aim-down-sights zoom also blends linearly in degrees rather than in tan(fov/2), so the apparent zoom speed is uneven.
evidence: reconstruction of CG_GetViewFov (deployFov = 55, EF_TURRET_MASK -> 55; viewFov - (viewFov - zoomFov) * frac)

description: The projection puts the far plane at infinity with ordinary (not reversed) depth: z/w approaches 0.9995 at infinity, so a 24-bit depth buffer has little precision left at distance and distant surfaces z-fight; r_znear (4 by default, at least 1) is the only control.
evidence: reconstruction of R_SetupProjection and InfinitePerspectiveMatrix (m22 = 0.99951171875, m32 = -zNear * 0.99951171875); r_znear's own description warns of z-fighting

description: Every aim-down-sights frame calls Sys_Milliseconds and stores the time in a function-local static (lastTime) that nothing reads.
evidence: reconstruction of CG_GetViewFov (static lastTime at 00E86AC0, guard $S1 at 00E86AC4; only written)
